newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices ease on poor mill demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices ease on poor mill demand.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Wednesday eased on sluggish mill demand and reports of widespread rain in producing centres, dealers said.

"Fresh arrivals however remained at a low ebb due to the tailend of the season as well as heavy rain in producing centres but unloading by local stockists kept supplies on the higher side," one broker said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 20/30 rupees at 1,020/1,060 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned slid by 10 rupees at 1,830/1,890 rupees per maund. F-414 slid by 10 rupees at 2,050/2,100 rupees per maund.

Gujarat varieties too fell on higher selling. Gujarat Kalyan dropped by 100/200 rupees at 14,000/14,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 (superior grade) fell by 500 rupees at 20,400/20,500 rupees per candy.
